generated_by: prism-parity:tools/generate-otel-span-attributes.php for php; the ports' own runners for ts and py. Every attribute map is execution output read back off an exporter — a hand-authored map would assert the author's model of the bridge rather than the bridge.
scope: The ROOT span of one generation, and only that. Step and tool spans are a separate value with a separate failure mode and are not covered here; a reader who takes this suite for whole-package coverage has made the mistake this repository's README warns about twice.

inputs.operation: One of Prism's own TelemetryOperation values -- text, structured, embeddings, image, stream. The NEUTRAL vocabulary the ecosystem already defines, so no language is handed a value pre-mapped into its own spelling.
inputs.finish_reason: One of Prism's own FinishReason values -- stop, tool-calls, length. Same reasoning.
inputs.capture_content: Whether the APPLICATION has content capture enabled. In the reference that is `prism.telemetry.capture_content`, which gates the events; in the ports it is the bridge's own `captureContent`. Two designs, one composed contract -- which is exactly what otel-0013 probes.

cases.title: a plain text generation
cases.notes: The control. Every attribute a generation always carries, with nothing optional set. If this row disagrees the mapping is wrong at the root and every other row is noise.

cases.title: an embeddings generation
cases.notes: Embeddings is the one operation all three agree is not a chat, so it is the row that proves the span-kind branch is reached at all rather than a constant.

cases.title: an image generation
cases.notes: An operation that is neither a chat nor an embedding. The reference has an explicit name for it and folds it into CHAIN; the ports pass the operation through and fall to a default kind.

cases.title: a streamed generation
cases.notes: Streaming is a transport, not a different operation, and a reader grouping spans by operation should not see a fourth category appear because the caller streamed.

cases.title: a structured generation
cases.notes: Structured output is still a chat to the GenAI conventions. Pinned so that a port cannot invent a fifth operation name for it.

cases.title: session and user ids, which Phoenix groups by
cases.notes: These two are the join keys a dashboard groups a conversation by. A language that spelled either differently would render one user's session as two.

cases.title: a reported cost
cases.notes: Only two providers report a real cost. The attribute is Prism-specific and namespaced, so it is exactly the sort of key a port could spell from memory.

cases.title: no reported cost, which is not a cost of zero
cases.notes: A span that spent money must stay distinguishable from one that did not. Writing 0.0 here would make a missing figure look like a free call, and no error would ever be raised.

cases.title: a finish reason that is not stop
cases.notes: A hyphenated reason, chosen because it is the one whose neutral spelling and whose PHP enum CASE NAME differ most visibly. A dashboard filtering on this value is the consumer that finds out.

cases.title: captured content, ascii
cases.notes: The first row where user content actually leaves the application. Pins the JSON ENCODING as much as the attribute key: the same payload has to serialise to the same bytes, or two services' spans never match on a search.

cases.title: captured content past the cap
cases.notes: The cap is a bound on what a hostile or simply large payload can do to a span and to the OTLP export. Ascii only, so the boundary is unambiguous and any disagreement here is in the cap arithmetic rather than in the encoding.

cases.title: captured content past the cap, multi-byte

input.prompt: 日本語のテキストです

cases.notes: The same cap against text that is not one byte per character. Bytes, UTF-16 code units and code points are three different rulers, and a cap measured with each gives three different strings from one input -- none of which errors.

cases.title: content reaching the bridge with capture OFF
cases.notes: THE SECURITY ROW. Capture is off and content arrives at the bridge anyway -- a replay, a hand-built event, a custom emitter, a second subscriber. The question is not what the application configured, it is whether the bridge itself refuses. Whichever way this row lands it is worth knowing, because the answer differs by language and neither side is obviously wrong until it is written down.
